title: Managing data with AzCopy and Azure Storage Explorer
learningObjective: Move data with AzCopy (copy, sync, server-side copies) and Storage Explorer using the right authorization, and troubleshoot failed transfers.

prerequisites.text: Moving files: AzCopy, Storage Explorer, File Sync (AZ-900)

foundation: AzCopy is a free command-line tool for copying data to, from and between storage accounts quickly.
Azure Storage Explorer is a free desktop app with a graphical view of your storage accounts, where you can upload, download and manage data. It uses AzCopy behind the scenes.
Both need permission to the data: either sign in with Microsoft Entra ID (and have a data role), or use a SAS token or account key.
engineer: Authorization: azcopy login (interactive, device code, managed identity or service principal) needs an Entra data role such as Storage Blob Data Contributor; Owner or Contributor alone is not enough. Alternatively, append a SAS to each URL.

Commands: azcopy copy (one-time copy; --recursive for folders), azcopy sync (copies only changed or new files based on last-modified time; --delete-destination=true mirrors deletions), azcopy make (create a container or share), azcopy remove, azcopy list, and azcopy jobs list/resume/show to resume failed transfers using the job's plan files.

Copies between storage accounts are server-side (Put Block From URL / Copy Blob from URL), so data does not flow through the client. Useful flags: --include-pattern, --exclude-pattern, --overwrite, --put-md5, --cap-mbps, --block-blob-tier.

Storage Explorer connects with Entra ID (subscription or resource), account name and key, SAS URL, or connection string, and also to Azurite (local emulator). It can manage access policies, generate SAS, change tiers, undelete soft-deleted blobs and work with Data Lake ACLs.
Firewall rules apply to both tools: the client IP or network must be allowed by the storage account.

animation.caption: Open the AzCopy tab: build copy and sync commands and see the authorization requirements.

example.title: Nightly mirror of a reports folder
body: A Windows server runs a scheduled task: azcopy login --identity (using the VM's managed identity, which holds Storage Blob Data Contributor), then azcopy sync C:\reports https://stcontoso.blob.core.windows.net/reports --recursive --delete-destination=true.
After a network outage, azcopy jobs resume finishes the interrupted job without re-uploading completed files.

prerequisites: AzCopy v10 or Storage Explorer installed
Network access to the storage endpoints
permissions: Storage Blob Data Contributor (or Reader for downloads) with azcopy login
Or a SAS with the required permissions
limits: Firewall rules apply to the client
portal: Storage account > Storage browser (in the portal) for quick uploads and downloads.
Download Storage Explorer from the portal's Open in Explorer link; sign in or attach with a SAS or connection string.
Container > Shared access tokens to create a SAS for AzCopy.
configuration.cli:
azcopy login
azcopy make "https://stcontoso.blob.core.windows.net/reports"
azcopy copy "C:\reports" "https://stcontoso.blob.core.windows.net/reports" --recursive
azcopy sync "C:\reports" "https://stcontoso.blob.core.windows.net/reports" --recursive --delete-destination=true
azcopy copy "https://stsource.blob.core.windows.net/reports?<SAS>" "https://stcontoso.blob.core.windows.net/reports?<SAS>" --recursive
azcopy jobs list
az storage blob upload-batch --account-name stcontoso --destination reports --source ./reports --auth-mode login
configuration.powershell:
# AzCopy is a standalone tool; Az.Storage cmdlets cover single-object operations
$ctx = New-AzStorageContext -StorageAccountName stcontoso -UseConnectedAccount
Set-AzStorageBlobContent -File .\report.csv -Container reports -Blob 2026/report.csv -Context $ctx
Start-AzStorageBlobCopy -SrcContainer reports -SrcBlob 2026/report.csv -DestContainer archive -DestBlob 2026/report.csv -Context $ctx

lab.objective: Build correct AzCopy commands and identify the authorization each needs.
steps: Open the AzCopy tab with azcopy login and no data role: read the predicted 403.
Tick the data role. Switch to sync and add --delete-destination.
Build an account-to-account copy using SAS and note that it is server-side.
expected: Login without a data role fails at transfer time

validation.text: Granted the identity a data role for azcopy login

failureScenarios: SAS missing list permission for sync
Client IP blocked by the firewall
lab.cost: AzCopy and Storage Explorer are free; transactions and egress are billed by Azure Storage.

troubleshooting.cause: Identity lacks a Storage Blob Data role.
troubleshooting.fix: Assign Storage Blob Data Contributor and wait for propagation.

troubleshooting.cause: Storage firewall blocks the client IP.
troubleshooting.fix: Add the IP or use an allowed network.
azcopy jobs resume <job-id> (with the same SAS if used).

troubleshooting.cause: Last-modified times differ (for example after a restore).
troubleshooting.fix: Use --compare-hash where supported, or accept a one-time full sync.

comparisons.difference: Offline transfer appliance for very large datasets or limited bandwidth; AzCopy is online.
Continuous sync and cloud tiering between Windows Servers and Azure Files; AzCopy runs one-off or scheduled transfers.

comparisons.service: AWS CLI s3 cp / s3 sync
comparisons.difference: Functionally similar commands for Amazon S3.

misconceptions.myth: Owner can upload with azcopy login.
Copying between two accounts downloads data to your PC.
misconceptions.reality: AzCopy uses server-side copy between accounts.

architectureDecisions: Use managed identities with azcopy login for scheduled jobs instead of embedding SAS tokens.
Use Data Box for multi-terabyte migrations over slow links.

steps.label: Many files
steps.title: Upload 50,000 files tonight
body: Clicking upload in the portal does not scale. You need a tool that copies in parallel and can resume.

steps.label: AzCopy
steps.title: AzCopy for scripts and big jobs
body: AzCopy is a free command-line tool. azcopy copy uploads, downloads or copies between accounts (server to server). azcopy sync makes a destination match a source. It runs on Windows, Linux and macOS, and is built into Azure Cloud Shell.

steps.label: Auth
steps.title: How AzCopy proves who you are
body: Sign in with azcopy login (Microsoft Entra ID; you need a data role such as Storage Blob Data Contributor), or append a SAS token to the URL. Azure Files supports SAS and, in newer versions, Entra ID.

callout.text: Owner or Contributor on the account is not enough for azcopy login uploads. You need a data role like Storage Blob Data Contributor.

steps.label: Explorer
steps.title: Storage Explorer for point and click
body: Azure Storage Explorer is a free desktop app to browse, upload, download and manage blobs, files, queues and tables. It uses AzCopy under the hood for transfers. In the portal, Storage browser does lighter jobs.

steps.label: Recap
steps.title: Moving data
recap: Sign in with Entra ID (data role) or a SAS

Storage browser in the portal for small jobs

handsOn.title: Upload files with AzCopy in Cloud Shell
handsOn.cost: Cents. A few small files in a Standard LRS account cost almost nothing; delete the account at the end.
before: Signed in at portal.azure.com as Owner of a subscription (a free or pay-as-you-go account works). Work in a resource group called rg-az104-lab.
If rg-az104-lab does not exist yet: search 'Resource groups' > Create > name rg-az104-lab, region UAE North (or any region near you) > Review + create > Create.
A storage account in rg-az104-lab: Standard performance, LRS redundancy, default settings. Name it st<yourinitials><number> (lowercase letters and numbers only, globally unique).

steps.do: Create a container named upload in the storage account.
Open the container > Settings > Shared access tokens. Permissions: Read, Add, Create, Write, List. Expiry: 2 hours. Generate and copy the Blob SAS URL.
Open Cloud Shell (the >_ icon at the top of the portal). Choose Bash. If asked about storage, choose 'No storage account required'.
steps.see: A Bash prompt in the browser.

steps.do: Type: mkdir files && for i in 1 2 3; do echo hello $i > files/f$i.txt; done
steps.see: Three small files created in the files folder.

steps.do: Type: azcopy copy 'files/*' '<paste the SAS URL here>'  (keep the single quotes).
steps.see: A job summary with 3 transfers completed.
steps.tip: Wrap the SAS URL in single quotes, because it contains & characters.

steps.see: The three files listed. You can also see them in the portal's container view.

steps.do: Optional: install Azure Storage Explorer on your PC, sign in, and browse the same container.
steps.see: The container and files in the desktop app.

check: Three files uploaded by AzCopy are visible in the container.
cleanup: When you finish for the day: Resource groups > rg-az104-lab > Delete resource group > type the name > Delete. This removes everything inside it.
